query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The type of incident (email, database, vpn) is not intervenable — you cannot decide to make an incident be a database issue — but it plausibly affects both how incidents are routed/handled and the resolution time, so it acts as a common-cause confounder.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The nature of the failure (connection failure, crash, access denied) is an immutable characteristic of the incident that jointly influences handling decisions and resolution time; a confounder, not a settable lever.

per_column.name: affected_system_tier
per_column.rationale: Which tier is affected is a structural property of the incident, not something an actor sets to reduce resolution time; it can influence both assignment and duration.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident recurs is an observed property that may correlate with both prioritization/handling and resolution time; not intervenable, so treated as a confounder.

per_column.name: is_assigned
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident is assigned is an intervenable operational lever — management can decide to assign incidents — and plausibly affects resolution time; a valid what-if treatment.

per_column.name: resolved_by_assignee
per_column.rationale: Whether the assignee ultimately resolved it is downstream of assignment and reflects the resolution process itself; it lies on the causal path rather than being a common cause, so it is a mediator/collider-like variable, not a confounder.

per_column.name: is_open_incident
per_column.rationale: Open/closed status is essentially a reflection of whether resolution has occurred; it is definitionally entangled with the outcome, not an independent treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Which agent is assigned is a genuinely intervenable assignment decision that can be set/changed and could affect resolution time; a valid intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: caller_id_group
per_column.rationale: The caller is not something the service org sets, but caller characteristics may relate to both routing and resolution time; a weak common-cause confounder.

judge.rationale: The added columns do set up a genuine interventional question: 'is_assigned' and 'assigned_agent' are settable operational levers that an actor can decide, satisfying the intervenability requirement (a). Several columns (incident_category, failure_mode, affected_system_tier, recurrence_signal, caller_id_group) function as common-cause confounders that are NOT named in the query, demonstrating the capability under test for requirement (b). However, quality is only moderate: some columns are mediators (resolved_by_assignee) or outcome reflections (is_open_incident) rather than confounders, and the assignment treatments themselves lack adjustment for agent workload/skill which would be the key confounders of the assigned_agent effect. The confounder set is plausible but not tightly tailored to blocking backdoor paths for the identified treatments.
